statement: In 31 of 39 books with text a spread ends on an unfinished line or a direct question answered on the next spread (e.g. 'And then…', 'Cat?', a sentence broken on 'BUT…' in I Can Do It!, a couplet whose rhyme arrives only after the turn in Sweet Dreams); the other 8 answer each spread within itself.

scope.population: contemporary open-licence picture books: Book Dash (35), African Storybook (2), StoryWeaver: Pratham Books (5), Room to Read (1); 2014-2026

analyst_note:
2026-10-14: Best Friends and An Unexpected Adventure (wordless) reviewed for this claim. Best Friends ends its penultimate spread on a question answered after the turn. The wordless book is not counted; its turns are visual (shape transitions).
2026-10-15: Book Dash: 5 support (Bathtub Safari strongest, 5 half-lines). African Storybook: Bohlale supports (count broken at 3 resumes at 47; cave eyes left open); Chicken and Millipede ends spreads on events, not open lines. StoryWeaver: Good Night, Monu's strongest turn is an ellipsis into a one-word reveal. Bedtime note (m004): in Monu the hook sits at 6/13 and the last third winds down with no open hooks. 2026-10-20: The Red Umbrella holds a wordless reveal across the p11-p12 turn; not counted (no text).
2026-10-28: +5 support, +3 counter. StoryWeaver: The Lost Ball (Room to Read) asks where the ball is at the end of each search spread and answers 'no' on the next; its turn breaks one sentence across two pages. Get Down, Rocky! (Pratham) ends p5 on an untold idea and p10 on a question to the reader answered by the last page. Book Dash: Let's Go Looking splits one sentence across p9-p10; Dudu's Hat and Clever Pig support. A Day Out (one exclamation per spread), Who Ate My Hat (each ask-and-deny answered inside its spread) and A House for Mouse (spreads end on a thank-you) are counterexamples. Goldfish Genius is wordless and not counted. Bedtime (m004): in A House for Mouse and Clever Pig the last third has no open hooks. Sources of the new works: Book Dash — A Day Out, Who Ate My Hat, Let's Go Looking, Dudu's Hat, Clever Pig, A House for Mouse, Goldfish Genius; StoryWeaver — Get Down, Rocky! (Pratham Books), The Lost Ball (Room to Read, translated from Bangla).
2026-10-28 older-book observation, NOT counted (SOURCES.md keeps populations apart): Millions of Cats (Internet Archive, 1928, Gág, study_only) weak counterexample (turns announce rather than leave a line open; boundaries are reconstructed, so not judged).
2026-11-13: +10 support, 0 counter. Weakest supports: A Trip to the Tap (one question, p10) and Banzi's Busy Bees (a promised trick, p5). Bedtime (m004): in Sweet Dreams the hooks stop at the waking page and the last two pages carry none. Sources of the new works: Book Dash — A Trip to the Tap (2023), Going Places (2025), AAAAAHHH!!!! Mmawe! (2024), Can We Eat a Rainbow? (2026), I Can Do It! (2026), Play with Me (2026), Banzi's Busy Bees (2025), Dance, Khuzwayo, Dance! (2023), Alex's Super Medicine (2022); StoryWeaver — Sweet Dreams (Pratham Books, year not shown).

magicpaper.suggested: Hypothesis for page-based stories: end some pages on a question or an open 'says...' and answer it after the turn.
